makaleler.baslik_en: Study Rationale, Enrollment Characteristics, and Central Review of Clinical Stage: The INTACT Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Study Rationale, Enrollment Characteristics, and Central Review of Clinical Stage: The INTACT Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.tur: Randomized Controlled Trial, Clinical Trial, Phase III
makaleler.ozet_en: IMPORTANCE: Trimodality therapy (TMT) is an established bladder-preservation approach for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). Accurate clinical staging remains challenging and may affect patient selection, trial design, and interpretation of outcomes. OBJECTIVE: To describe the design, accrual, and baseline characteristics of the Phase III Randomized Trial of Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy With or Without Atezolizumab in Localized Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (INTACT) trial and evaluate agreement between site-reported and centrally reviewed clinical stage and the prevalence of high-risk disease features.

makaleler.baslik_en: Multilevel Mobility Intervention and Life-Space Mobility in Older Hospitalized Medical Patients: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Multilevel Mobility Intervention and Life-Space Mobility in Older Hospitalized Medical Patients: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.ozet_en: IMPORTANCE: Low mobility is common during an acute hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes, such as loss of independence and death. Previous interventions that were successful in increasing hospital mobility required resources that are not available in everyday clinical practice, limiting their scalability. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether the theory-informed Intervention to Increase Mobility in Older Hospitalized Medical Patients (INTOMOB) improves life-space mobility at 30 days in older hospitalized medical patients.

makaleler.baslik_en: Resistance Exercise Training for Depressive Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Resistance Exercise Training for Depressive Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression Analysis.
makaleler.ozet_en: IMPORTANCE: Resistance exercise training (RET) has established antidepressant effects compared with inactive control conditions; however, its effects vs active comparisons remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association of RET efficacy with active and inactive comparisons for depressive symptoms and explore variability across moderators. DATA SOURCES: Published articles were identified using Google Scholar, MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, and PsycInfo from inception to July 7, 2025. STUDY SELECTION: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) with at least 3 weeks of RET or any non-RET comparison and a validated depressive symptom measure at baseline and at least 3 weeks were included.
